slides.title: One save *wipes out* the other
slides.voiceover: Two users change the same order. One save wipes out the other.
slides.spoken: Two users change the same order. One save wipes out the other.

slides.label: THE FIX
slides.heading: A *lock object*
slides.body: Like the occupied sign on a meeting room door: one user edits, everyone else waits.
slides.voiceover: No error, no warning. The data is just wrong. The fix is a lock object. Think of the occupied sign on a meeting room door.
slides.spoken: No error, no warning. The data is just wrong. The fix is a lock object. Think of the occupied sign on a meeting room door.

slides.heading: Create it in *SE11*
slides.note: activation creates ENQUEUE_ and DEQUEUE_ modules
slides.voiceover: Create it in SE11. The name must start with E Z. Add the table, for example VBAK, and pick write lock.
slides.spoken: Create it in SE11. The name must start with EZ. Add the table, for example VBAK, and pick write lock.

slides.heading: Lock *before* you change
slides.code:
CALL FUNCTION 'ENQUEUE_EZ_ORDER'
  EXPORTING vbeln = lv_vbeln
  EXCEPTIONS foreign_lock = 1 OTHERS = 2.
IF sy-subrc <> 0.
  MESSAGE 'Order is locked' TYPE 'E'.
ENDIF.
slides.voiceover: Activation creates two function modules. Call ENQUEUE before you change the order. If sy-subrc isn't zero, someone else holds the lock. Stop, and tell the user.
slides.spoken: Activation creates two function modules. Call ENQUEUE before you change the order. If sy-subrc isn't zero, someone else holds the lock. Stop, and tell the user.

slides.heading: The *ritual*
slides.label: EVERY TIME
slides.voiceover: Then lock, change, save, unlock with DEQUEUE. Every time.
slides.spoken: Then lock, change, save, unlock with DEQUEUE. Every time.

slides.label: CHECK IT
slides.heading: See locks in *SM12*
slides.title: Lock Entries
slides.voiceover: SM12 shows every open lock, with the user, the object and the key.
slides.spoken: SM12 shows every open lock, with the user, the object and the key.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.heading: Locked, but *not checked*

bad.title: Ignore sy-subrc
bad.sub: you still overwrite the other user

good.title: Check sy-subrc
good.sub: locked? stop and tell the user

slides.voiceover: Common mistake: calling ENQUEUE but ignoring sy-subrc. Then you still overwrite the other user. Always check it.
slides.spoken: Common mistake: calling ENQUEUE but ignoring sy-subrc. Then you still overwrite the other user. Always check it.

slides.title: Where do *columns* come from?
slides.voiceover: Every column of your table starts here. Last time we learned the data browser setting. Now, the fields tab.
slides.spoken: Every column of your table starts here. Last time we learned the data browser setting. Now, the fields tab.

slides.label: WHY
slides.heading: Fields = *columns*
slides.body: Each line on the Fields tab is one column of the database table.
slides.voiceover: Why? A table is only rows and columns. The fields tab is where you define the columns.
slides.spoken: Why? A table is only rows and columns. The fields tab is where you define the columns.

slides.heading: The *Fields* tab
slides.voiceover: Open SCARR in SE11 and click the Fields tab. Each line has a field name, a key flag, initial values and a data element.
slides.spoken: Open SCARR in SE11 and click the Fields tab. Each line has a field name, a key flag, initial values and a data element.

slides.label: EXAMPLE
slides.heading: *SCARR*, field by field
slides.title: SCARR · Fields
slides.voiceover: Here are SCARR's real fields. MANDT, the client. CARRID, the airline code. CARRNAME, the airline name. CURRCODE, the currency. URL, the website.
slides.spoken: Here are SCARR's real fields. MANDT, the client. CARRID, the airline code. CARRNAME, the airline name. CURRCODE, the currency. URL, the website.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.heading: Predefined type *everywhere*

bad.title: Predefined Type
bad.sub: no labels, no F1 help, no reuse

good.title: Data element
good.sub: labels, F1 help, one change updates all

slides.voiceover: Common mistake: typing the type and length straight into the field with predefined type. It works, but you lose the labels and F1 help. Use a data element instead.
slides.spoken: Common mistake: typing the type and length straight into the field with predefined type. It works, but you lose the labels and F1 help. Use a data element instead.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: One line = *one column*
slides.body: Field name + Key + data element = a column with a meaning.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: one line on the fields tab is one column, and a data element gives it meaning.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: one line on the fields tab is one column, and a data element gives it meaning.

slides.title: Why did my *INSERT* do nothing?
slides.voiceover: Insert the same row twice, and nothing happens. Last time we learned the fields tab. Now, the primary key.
slides.spoken: Insert the same row twice, and nothing happens. Last time we learned the fields tab. Now, the primary key.

slides.label: NEW TERM
slides.heading: The *primary key*
slides.body: Primary key = the key fields that identify exactly one row. No two rows may share them.
slides.voiceover: Why? The primary key is the set of fields that makes every row unique. No two rows can share it.
slides.spoken: Why? The primary key is the set of fields that makes every row unique. No two rows can share it.

slides.heading: Tick *Key*
slides.voiceover: On the fields tab, tick Key for each key field. Key fields come first, together, at the top of the table.
slides.spoken: On the fields tab, tick Key for each key field. Key fields come first, together, at the top of the table.

slides.label: MANDT
slides.heading: *MANDT* goes first
slides.body: Client-dependent table: MANDT is the first key field, so client 100 and client 200 keep separate rows.
slides.voiceover: MANDT comes first in a client-dependent table. It's the client, so each client has its own rows.
slides.spoken: MANDT comes first in a client-dependent table. It's the client, so each client has its own rows.

slides.heading: Same key *twice*
slides.code:
ls_air = VALUE #( carrid = 'LH' carrname = 'Lufthansa' ).
INSERT ztairline FROM ls_air.
" key LH exists already
IF sy-subrc = 4.
  " duplicate key: nothing inserted
ENDIF.
slides.voiceover: Now insert a row whose key already exists. No dump. sy-subrc is four, and the row is not written.
slides.spoken: Now insert a row whose key already exists. No dump. sy-subrc is 4, and the row is not written.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.heading: Assuming it *saved*
slides.voiceover: Common mistake: not checking sy-subrc after insert. The program carries on as if the row was saved. Check it every time.
slides.spoken: Common mistake: not checking sy-subrc after insert. The program carries on as if the row was saved. Check it every time.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Key = *unique row*
slides.body: Key fields first, MANDT at the top, and check sy-subrc after INSERT.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: the key makes each row unique, and MANDT comes first.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: the key makes each row unique, and MANDT comes first.
